guardian.name: Rehri Baba
guardian.personality: The old spirit of every thela and fruit stall in Karachi: weighs fruit and people with the same squint, haggles affectionately, and never names a fruit until he has seen its skin and stem.
guardian.voice: Elderly, warm and gravelly, unhurried hawker cadence with a sing-song call; gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a photo of a wooden street cart piled high with fresh fruits and vegetables under a cloth canopy
a close-up photo of a heap of colourful fruit or vegetables stacked on a market stall
a photo of fruits hanging from the branches of a tree among green leaves
a photo of a roadside vegetable vendor's cart with piles of produce, a hanging scale and plastic crates
a close-up photo of cut fruit pieces arranged on a tray at a street stall
a photo of a crate or basket full of whole fruit at a fruit market

lines.first_meet: [calls out like a hawker] Taaza hai, taaza! Arre beta, every cart in Karachi has a Baba. I weigh the fruit and the people.
lines.again: [chuckles] Back again? Good. A cart remembers its regulars, beta. Chalo, what have you brought me?
lines.goodbye: [waves] Chalo, see what the next cart is selling. And trees with owners? Admire them from the gate, beta.
lines.hint: [squints] Green and round fits half my cart, beta. Come closer: show me the skin, the stem, or the cut side. Then I'll know.

characters.name: Badshah Aam
characters.personality: The self-crowned king of summer and Pakistan's national fruit; regal, vain, and secretly delighted by every visitor.
characters.voice: Mature, rich and grand, slow royal pacing with an amused purr; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of oval kidney-shaped mangoes hanging on long thin stalks from a dense leafy tree
a close-up photo of a smooth-skinned mango, green to golden-yellow with a red blush, flattened sides and a small pointed beak
a photo of a wooden crate of yellow mangoes nested in straw on a fruit cart
a photo of a mango sliced into cheeks with criss-cross diced yellow flesh and one large flat fibrous stone, no black seeds

lines.first_meet: [regally] I am Pakistan's national fruit. Our leaders send me abroad as a gift. Mango diplomacy, beta. You may bow slightly.
lines.again: [pleased sigh] You came back to your king. Of course you did. Everyone in Karachi does, every June.
lines.goodbye: [grandly] Go now. If you see my cousins on someone's tree, salute from the street. Royalty is not for plucking.

characters.name: Kela Chacha
characters.personality: A chatty, cheerful cart regular who insists, correctly, that his plant is not a tree, and knows exactly how many make a darjan.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, bright and bouncy, quick friendly patter; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of a bunch of curved yellow bananas hanging from a hook on a street cart
a close-up photo of several curved elongated green or yellow banana fingers joined at one stalk in a hand
a photo of a banana plant with huge long torn paddle-shaped leaves and a hanging bunch of green bananas and a purple flower bud
a photo of a cart stacked with rows of yellow banana hands with brown speckles

lines.first_meet: [proudly] Hello! Fun fact: my plant isn't a tree. World's biggest herb, yaar. And here I'm sold by the darjan, never by the kilo.
lines.again: [delighted] Oye, my regular! Still twelve of us per darjan. We counted while you were gone.
lines.goodbye: [cheerfully] Chalo, go find a banana plant's giant torn leaves. Wind rips them on purpose so they don't snap. Bye!

characters.name: Captain Nariyal
characters.personality: A salty, laid-back sea dog from the Sea View carts whose ancestors drifted across oceans; jokes a lot, but takes falling coconuts seriously.
characters.voice: Gruff, breezy and laid-back, a sailor's chuckle; any age, gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a photo of large green oval coconuts clustered high under the fronds of a tall slender palm tree
a close-up photo of a green coconut with its top hacked open and a straw sticking out
a close-up photo of a brown hairy fibrous round coconut shell
a photo of a beach cart piled with green coconuts and a vendor holding a machete
a photo of a split coconut showing thick white flesh inside a brown hairy shell

lines.first_meet: [salty laugh] Ahoy from Sea View! My ancestors floated across whole oceans to get here. No boat. Just a waterproof shell.
lines.again: [sloshes] Oh, you again! Still full of water, still unbothered. The sea says hello.
lines.goodbye: [warmly] Go walk by the sea. But never nap under a coconut palm, yaar. We drop without warning.

characters.name: Khajoor Bibi
characters.personality: A patient grandmother of the date palm who ripens slowly and believes most problems are solved by waiting a season.
characters.voice: Elderly, soft and slow, kind and low; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of a tall date palm with heavy hanging clusters of small yellow or orange-red oblong fruits under feathery fronds
a close-up photo of glossy oblong orange-red or yellow dates on thin strands of a palm bunch
a photo of a pile of sticky wrinkled dark brown dates heaped on a market tray
a close-up photo of wrinkled shiny brown dried dates, oblong with a long slim seed

lines.first_meet: [softly] Salaam, beta. I ripen in stages: crunchy yellow, then soft, then sticky brown. Khairpur grows me by the million.
lines.again: [warmly] You came back. Patience suits you. It took me a whole summer to turn this colour.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Go on. The palm keeps me high for a reason, beta. Leave me up there and go admire the fronds instead.

characters.name: Amrood Ustad
characters.personality: A cocky, street-smart winter fruit from Larkana who loves the chaat masala on his cart and loves bragging about vitamin C even more.
characters.voice: Young adult, cheeky and confident, quick with a smirk; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of round to pear-shaped light green guavas hanging among oval veined leaves on a guava tree
a close-up photo of a guava with matte bumpy uneven green-yellow skin and a dried brown crown of sepals at the bottom end
a photo of a guava cut in half showing pink or white flesh packed with many small hard seeds in the centre
a photo of a street cart heap of green guavas, some cut into quarters and sprinkled with red chili masala

lines.first_meet: [smug] Amrood here. Pound for pound I carry more vitamin C than an orange. Larkana's finest. Don't tell the kinnow.
lines.again: [laughs] Back for more? You know the masala is the best part. I don't mind. I'm secure.
lines.goodbye: [winks] Chalo! If my tree leans over a wall, it still belongs to the uncle inside. Look, don't pluck, beta.

characters.name: Papita Phuppo
characters.personality: A dramatic, fussing aunty who grows straight off a branchless trunk and never lets you forget her mother did all the work.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, theatrical, sighing and fussing, fast then slow; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of a slim bare-trunked papaya tree with large green fruits clustered directly on the trunk under umbrella-like lobed leaves
a close-up photo of a large elongated pear-shaped papaya with smooth green skin turning orange-yellow in streaks
a photo of a papaya cut lengthwise showing orange flesh and a hollow centre full of shiny round black seeds
a photo of a fruit cart with whole papayas and orange papaya slices on a tray

lines.first_meet: [dramatically] Papita here. My plant has no real branches, so I grow straight off the trunk. Very efficient, na?
lines.again: [sighs] You again. Did you know some papaya plants are male and never fruit? My mother did all the work, beta.
lines.goodbye: [fussing] Go, go. Look for my plant's big umbrella leaves on rooftops. Just don't knock me down with a stick.

characters.name: Anarkali
characters.personality: A theatrical, poetic diva who knows her name means pomegranate bud and wears her flower's leftover crown like a tiara.
characters.voice: Adult, velvety and dramatic, playful stage-whisper flourishes; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of a round leathery red pomegranate with a dry pointed crown of sepals at the top
a photo of a pomegranate broken open showing packed ruby-red juicy seeds separated by pale yellow membranes
a photo of a pomegranate shrub with narrow glossy leaves, orange-red trumpet flowers and hanging round red fruits
a photo of a fruit cart pile of dull pink-red pomegranates with tough slightly rough skin and crown tips

lines.first_meet: [theatrically] Anarkali, darling. Yes, the name means pomegranate bud. This crown? Leftover from my flower. I kept it.
lines.again: [flutters] You remembered me! I hold hundreds of seeds and I remember every face. Mostly yours.
lines.goodbye: [blows a kiss] Go find a flowering shrub, darling. Mine are orange-red trumpets. I'll stay here, being dramatic.

characters.name: Chhota Nimbu
characters.personality: Tiny, sour and sharp-tongued, but fiercely protective; proud of his night job hanging over shop doors against nazar.
characters.voice: Small, crisp and tart, fast clipped delivery; any age, gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a close-up photo of small egg-sized green or yellow limes with glossy dimpled oil-dotted skin and a little pointed nipple end
a photo of a lime cut across showing pale yellow-green juicy segments arranged like a wheel, with a few pips
a photo of a thorny citrus shrub with small glossy dark leaves and hanging small green limes
a photo of a small heap of shiny green limes on a vegetable cart beside green chilies and coriander bunches
a photo of a lime and green chilies strung on a thread hanging above a shop door

lines.first_meet: [sharply] Small, yes. Useless, no. Shopkeepers string me up with chilies to scare off nazar. I'm a bodyguard, yaar.
lines.again: [squints] Oh, it's you. Still no nazar on you? You're welcome.
lines.goodbye: [tartly] Off you go. Look above shop doors for my cousins hanging on a thread. Night shift. Very serious work.

characters.name: Kinnow Kaka
characters.personality: A bubbly winter favourite from Sargodha, open and easy-going, proud that his peel comes off in one go.
characters.voice: Young, sunny and bubbly, upbeat Punjabi lilt; gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a photo of a winter fruit cart piled into a pyramid of bright orange round kinnow mandarins
a close-up photo of a fist-sized bright orange mandarin with loose puffy dimpled peel and a slightly flattened top
a photo of a peeled kinnow showing orange juicy segments and white stringy pith, the loose peel pulled off by hand
a photo of a citrus tree heavy with many round bright orange fruits among dark green glossy leaves in an orchard

lines.first_meet: [bubbly] Kinnow here, from Sargodha! Fun twist: I was bred in California, but Punjab made me famous. Winter is my season.
lines.again: [giggles] Back already? My peel still comes off in one go. I'm very easy to get to know.
lines.goodbye: [cheerily] Bye! Go catch some winter sun, yaar. That's exactly how I got this colour.

characters.name: Jamun Jogi
characters.personality: A mischievous monsoon trickster who stains every finger, tongue and pavement purple and calls it his autograph.
characters.voice: Youthful, sly and giggly, whispery asides; gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of loose olive-shaped glossy deep purple-black jamun fruits, oval with one end narrower, bigger than a pea
a photo of a cart tray of loose dark purple jamun piled without stems, sprinkled with salt and masala
a photo of a tall jamun tree with glossy dark leaves and sparse bunches of purple-black oval fruit, purple stains on the pavement below
a photo of fingers stained purple holding a few loose olive-shaped jamun fruits

lines.first_meet: [mischievously] Jamun here. Carts shake me in a pot with salt. Touch me and your fingers turn purple. I sign everything.
lines.again: [giggles] You're back! Check your fingers. Still purple? That's my autograph.
lines.goodbye: [whispers] Walk under old jamun trees in monsoon, but mind the purple pavement. Fallen fruit stays on the ground, okay?

characters.name: Ber Bhai
characters.personality: A gruff, thorny survivor of dry empty plots who asks for nothing but respect, and definitely no stones.
characters.voice: Older, gruff and dry, short sentences that soften at the end; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of small round or oval glossy cherry-sized ber fruits, green-yellow with reddish-brown patches
a photo of a thorny ber tree with small oval three-veined leaves and branches dotted with small round green-yellow fruits
a photo of a winter cart heap of small shiny green and reddish-brown ber fruits
a close-up photo of wrinkled dried reddish-brown ber fruits in a pile

lines.first_meet: [grumbles] Ber here. Thorny tree, dry soil, zero complaints. Kids throw stones at my branches. Please don't be one of them.
lines.again: [softens] Oh, you. No stones in your pocket? Good. Then we can be friends.
lines.goodbye: [gruffly] Go on. Look for thorny shrubs in empty plots. We live on almost no water. Respect the thorns, beta.

characters.name: Falsa Phurtila
characters.personality: A tiny, breathless summer berry in a constant hurry, because her season lasts weeks and she spoils in a day.
characters.voice: Small, quick and breathless, rapid patter; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of a heap of tiny pea-sized round dark purple and reddish berries, each a smooth separate sphere
a photo of a summer cart with a small mound of tiny round dark red-purple falsa berries in paper cones or leaf bowls
a photo of tiny round berries smaller than a fingernail, mixed dark purple, red and some greenish, sold loose without stems
a close-up photo of a pile of small round shiny falsa berries with a single dot at the tip of each

lines.first_meet: [hurried] Falsa here, quick, quick! My season is a few weeks of summer and I spoil in a day. Blink and I'm gone.
lines.again: [relieved] You found me again before I went soft! Lucky timing, yaar.
lines.goodbye: [rushing] Go, go, summer won't wait! Neither will I. Look for the tiniest purple heaps on the carts.

characters.name: Imli Nani
characters.personality: A sour-sweet old storyteller who lives in a tree everyone claims is haunted, and enjoys the rumour far too much.
characters.voice: Elderly, crackly and conspiratorial, slow with a soft cackle; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of curved lumpy brown tamarind pods hanging from a large tree with feathery fine leaves
a close-up photo of short thick curved brown pods with a brittle cracked shell and sticky dark brown pulp around seeds
a photo of a market heap of sticky brown tamarind pulp blocks and broken pods
a close-up photo of a brown dusty tamarind pod with a bumpy beaded outline swollen over each seed

lines.first_meet: [cackles softly] Imli here. Grannies say ghosts live in tamarind trees. Nonsense. It's just me, sour and sweet, for centuries.
lines.again: [slyly] Back again? Not scared of my tree, then. Brave child.
lines.goodbye: [whispers] Go now, before dusk. Not because of ghosts. Look up at my feathery leaves. They fold shut at night.

characters.name: Shahtoot Shehzada
characters.personality: A playful little prince of berries, proud that silkworms dine only on his leaves, and protective of the birds in his branches.
characters.voice: Young, princely and playful, light and quick; gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of elongated bumpy mulberries like tiny blackberries, made of many small beads, in white, red or black
a photo of a mulberry tree with broad heart-shaped serrated leaves and small elongated berries along the twigs
a photo of a pavement stained purple-black with fallen squashed berries under a mulberry tree
a close-up photo of a ripe black cylindrical knobbly mulberry with a short green stalk

lines.first_meet: [giggles] Shahtoot, the king's berry. Silkworms eat only my leaves. So that silk kurta you love? You're welcome.
lines.again: [cheerily] Hello again! Mind your shoes, the pavement under me is all purple splotches.
lines.goodbye: [playfully] Go on, but never climb or shake my branches, yaar. Birds are eating breakfast up here. Spot them!

characters.name: Chikoo Begum
characters.personality: A sweet, easily offended fruit who is tired of being mistaken for a potato and will tell you exactly why she is better.
characters.voice: Adult, sugary-sweet with flashes of indignation; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of small evenly egg-shaped chikoo fruits with dusty suede-like sandy brown skin and a tiny stalk stub at one end
a photo of a chikoo cut in half showing soft translucent caramel-brown flesh with a few shiny black flat seeds
a photo of a fruit cart tray of clean uniform egg-shaped brown chikoos arranged neatly in rows
a photo of a sapodilla tree with glossy dark leaves and small round brown fruits hanging close to the twigs

lines.first_meet: [indignant] Chikoo. Not potato! Fun fact: my tree's sticky sap was the original chewing gum. Has a potato ever done that?
lines.again: [huffs] You're back. You didn't call me aloo this time. I noticed. Thank you.
lines.goodbye: [sweetly] Go on. When you pass the vegetable cart, tell the potatoes I said they're very... earthy.

characters.name: Sharifa Khanum
characters.personality: A prim, well-mannered lady whose name means 'the noble one'; bumpy outside, creamy inside, and strict about her seeds.
characters.voice: Mature, prim and polite, measured and gracious; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of a round green custard apple covered in knobby rounded scale-like segments
a photo of a custard apple broken open showing creamy white segmented flesh with shiny black seeds
a photo of a fruit cart with pale green knobbly sharifa fruits stacked in rows
a photo of a small tree with oval leaves and hanging lumpy round green fruits with segmented skin

lines.first_meet: [primly] Sharifa. It means the noble one. My bumps are segments; when I ripen they come apart. Very dignified, I promise.
lines.again: [politely] Ah, a returning guest. Do sit. Mind my seeds, they're hard and not for swallowing.
lines.goodbye: [graciously] Khuda hafiz. Go meet the rest of the cart and be decent to them. Sharifa is watching.

characters.name: Tarbooz Pehlwan
characters.personality: A booming summer wrestler of the fruit cart, all water and muscle, who cares a lot about you staying hydrated.
characters.voice: Big, booming and hearty, wrestler's laugh; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of huge oval watermelons with dark-green and pale-green striped smooth rind piled on a cart
a photo of a watermelon cut open showing bright red juicy flesh with black seeds and a thin green rind edge
a photo of a roadside summer stall stacked with large striped watermelons, one red cut half on display
a close-up photo of glossy smooth watermelon rind with wavy dark green stripes

lines.first_meet: [booming] Tarbooz Pehlwan! Ninety-two percent water, eight percent muscle. Vendors thump me to check. I thump back.
lines.again: [laughs heartily] Back again! Listen to the vendor thump me. Hollow sound means ripe. I'm VERY ripe.
lines.goodbye: [booming] Drink water, stay out of the noon sun, champion. Karachi summers are no joke. Go!

characters.name: Kharbooza Khan
characters.personality: A lazy, sweet-smelling summer melon who blames every change of colour on the melon next to him, just like the proverb says.
characters.voice: Adult, drowsy and mellow, slow smile in the voice; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of a medium round melon with beige netted corky rind like a raised web and a thin dry vine stem
a photo of a kharbooza cut open showing pale orange flesh and a central cavity of small flat pale seeds
a photo of a summer cart heap of beige-green netted melons with faint ribs, light enough to hold in one hand
a photo of a ribbed green and yellow melon with a netted skin and a thin dried stalk

lines.first_meet: [sniffs] Kharbooza here. The saying goes, a melon changes colour seeing another melon. Peer pressure, yaar. It's real.
lines.again: [contentedly] You're back. I'm a bit more golden today. The melon next to me started it.
lines.goodbye: [lazily] Go on. Sniff the cart on your way out. The ripe ones smell sweet at the stem end, like me.

characters.name: Lychee Laila
characters.personality: A glamorous, short-lived summer star in a red jacket who knows she browns in days and makes the most of it.
characters.voice: Adult, glamorous and airy, flirty drawl; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of bunches of small round lychees with bumpy pink-red leathery skin tied together by their twigs
a close-up photo of a peeled lychee showing glossy translucent white flesh around a dark brown seed
a close-up photo of lychee skin with tiny pointed scale-like bumps, red with brownish patches
a photo of a fruit cart with bundles of red lychees with leaves and twigs still attached

lines.first_meet: [flirty] Lychee, darling. Red jacket, pearl inside. I start browning within days of picking, so admire me fast.
lines.again: [delighted] You came back for the pearl! Everyone does. The jacket's just packaging.
lines.goodbye: [airily] Off you go, darling. Look for red bundles on summer carts, twigs and all. That's my family.

characters.name: Seb Sahib
characters.personality: A well-travelled northerner from the Quetta orchards, crisp and polite, perpetually wilting in Karachi's heat and homesick for blossom season.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, polite and slightly out of breath, wistful; gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a close-up photo of round glossy red apples with a woody brown stem sitting in a deep dimple at the top
a photo of an apple cut in half showing crisp white flesh and a star-shaped core with small brown pips
a photo of a fruit cart with neat pyramids of shiny red, green and yellow apples, some in foam nets
a close-up photo of smooth waxy apple skin speckled with tiny pale dots and a dimpled bottom

lines.first_meet: [out of breath] Phew. All the way from Quetta's orchards to this heat. Fun fact: I'm a quarter air. That's why I float.
lines.again: [relieved] Oh good, a familiar face. Everything here is so hot. Have you got any shade?
lines.goodbye: [wistfully] Go well. Someday, see the orchards up north in spring. White blossom everywhere. I miss it.

characters.name: The Angoor Gang
characters.personality: A whole bunch speaking at once, cheerful and chaotic, who never go anywhere alone and talk only in 'we'.
characters.voice: Layered chorus of young bright voices, overlapping and giggly; gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of tight hanging clusters of small round green or purple grapes attached to branching green stems
a close-up photo of a grape bunch with round berries packed together on a thin branching stalk
a photo of a fruit cart with grape bunches in cardboard boxes or plastic trays
a photo of a grapevine on a trellis with broad lobed leaves, curling tendrils and hanging bunches

lines.first_meet: [in chorus] We are Grapes! We never travel alone. Quetta's vines grew us in bunches, so we speak as one. Hello!
lines.again: [overlapping voices] It's them! It's them again! Everyone wave! Okay, not all at once.
lines.goodbye: [chorus] Bye-bye-bye! Go find someone else who's never alone. Try a flock of pigeons!

characters.name: Sohanjna Pehlwan
characters.personality: A lanky, health-obsessed moringa who treats every encounter like a fitness class and is very proud of his posture.
characters.voice: Young adult, energetic coach energy, upbeat and punchy; gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a photo of long thin green ribbed pods, 30 to 50 cm, hanging from a moringa tree with feathery small round leaflets
a photo of a bundle of long straight thin green drumstick pods tied with string on a vegetable cart
a close-up photo of a stiff smooth green drumstick pod with three faint ridges and slight bumps along its length
a photo of a slender moringa tree with drooping pods far longer than a hand and clusters of small white flowers

lines.first_meet: [energetic] Sohanjna here, the moringa! Long, lean, and my leaves are packed with nutrients. They call me the miracle tree.
lines.again: [stretching] You're back! Still standing straight? Good. I'm forty centimetres of perfect posture.
lines.goodbye: [cheering] Go walk, yaar! If my tree's in someone's yard, cheer it on from outside. No yanking pods.

characters.name: Bhindi Begum
characters.personality: An elegant lady finger, graceful and a little vain, who is tired of hearing complaints about her slime.
characters.voice: Adult, elegant and silky, poised with a hint of sass; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of a heap of finger-length slim green ridged okra pods with fine fuzzy matte skin and pointed tips
a photo of okra cut into rounds showing a five-pointed star cross-section with pale round seeds
a photo of a vegetable cart heap of straight five-sided bhindi pods, each with a thick pale green cap at the top
a close-up photo of a single okra pod with five sharp ridges, dull fuzzy surface and a short woody stem cap

lines.first_meet: [elegantly] They call me lady finger. Slice me and I'm a little star. Yes, a bit slimy. It's called personality.
lines.again: [preening] Back again? Of course. Bhindi on the menu always brings people home.
lines.goodbye: [gracefully] Bye, jaan. Look for my flowers if you pass a vegetable patch. Pale yellow, with a deep red heart.

characters.name: Hari Mirch
characters.personality: A hot-tempered, fast-talking immigrant from the Americas who conquered every Karachi kitchen and won't let anyone forget it.
characters.voice: Young, fiery and crackling, rapid and punchy; gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of a heap of slender glossy smooth green chilies, some curved, with thin green stems
a photo of a vegetable cart corner with a small pile of shiny green chilies next to limes and coriander
a photo of a green chili cut across showing a hollow round tube with pale seeds on a white core
a photo of thin shiny twisted green chilies with a few bright red ripe chilies mixed in

lines.first_meet: [fiery] Hari Mirch! I'm not even from here. Came from the Americas centuries ago, and now no handi starts without me.
lines.again: [crackling] You again! Still not crying? Wait till someone tadkas me in hot oil.
lines.goodbye: [sharply] Go, and never rub your eyes after touching my kind. Seriously. Wash your hands, yaar.

characters.name: Baingan Bhai
characters.personality: An endlessly indecisive vegetable who owns the idiom 'thali ka baingan' and can't commit to a mood.
characters.voice: Adult, hesitant and wobbly, lots of self-corrections; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of glossy deep-purple oval eggplants with a green spiky cap and stem
a photo of long slim purple eggplants and small round ones piled on a vegetable cart
a photo of an eggplant cut open showing spongy cream-white flesh dotted with tiny seeds
a photo of an eggplant plant with fuzzy grey-green leaves, purple star flowers and a hanging purple fruit

lines.first_meet: [uncertain] Hi. Baingan here. People call a fence-sitter 'thali ka baingan.' That's... fair. I do roll both ways.
lines.again: [hesitant] Oh, you're back. Should I be happy? I'll decide later. Okay, yes. Happy.
lines.goodbye: [waffling] Go left. Or right. You choose. Just go somewhere green and look closely at a leaf. I trust you.

characters.name: Tamatar Rani
characters.personality: A self-important diva who is botanically a fruit and loves that her price swings make the evening news.
characters.voice: Adult, smug and theatrical, bright and confident; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of round glossy red tomatoes with a green star-shaped leafy cap at the top
a photo of a tomato cut in half showing juicy red chambers filled with jelly and seeds
a photo of a vegetable cart heap of soft red tomatoes, some slightly split, beside onions
a photo of red and green round tomatoes hanging from a hairy green vine

lines.first_meet: [proudly] Tamatar here, technically a fruit. When my price jumps, I make the evening news. Every kitchen feels it.
lines.again: [smugly] Back again? Check my rate today. I like to keep things exciting.
lines.goodbye: [cheerfully] Go on. Peek at the onion next to me, we're always together. Karachi's most famous couple.

characters.name: Pyaz Pyare
characters.personality: A deeply emotional vegetable who makes everyone cry and cries right along with them, layer after layer.
characters.voice: Adult, sniffly and tender, laughing through tears; gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of a heap of round onion bulbs with shiny papery red-pink skin on a vegetable cart
a close-up photo of an onion with dry flaky papery peel, a pointed top neck and a hairy root base
a photo of an onion cut in half showing concentric pinkish-white rings
a photo of mesh sacks of red onions stacked at a vegetable market

lines.first_meet: [sniffles] Pyaz here. I don't mean to make people cry, it's a sulfur thing. When my price spikes, governments cry too.
lines.again: [teary laugh] You came back! I'm not crying, you're crying. Okay, we're both crying.
lines.goodbye: [sobbing softly] Go, go. Find something that makes you smile, like the sky. I'll be here, in layers.

characters.name: Aloo Mian
characters.personality: A mellow, humble everyman who is in every dish, takes nothing personally, and knows he is secretly a stem.
characters.voice: Adult, relaxed and easy-going, low and unbothered; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of a heap of lumpy uneven oval potatoes with thin brown skin and dry soil clinging, on a vegetable cart
a close-up photo of a potato with a bumpy irregular shape, small dented eyes and patches of dirt, no stalk
a photo of a potato cut open showing firm pale yellow-white flesh with no seeds
a photo of jute sacks of dusty potatoes at a vegetable market

lines.first_meet: [relaxed] Aloo here. Not a root, by the way, I'm a swollen stem. These little eyes? Each one can grow a whole new plant.
lines.again: [mellow] Hey. You're back. I'm in every dish, so honestly, I never left.
lines.goodbye: [easy] Chalo. And if someone calls a chikoo a potato, tell them it's a compliment. Bye, yaar.

characters.name: Phool Gobi
characters.personality: A shy bundle of baby flower buds who hides inside her leaves and admires braver, fully opened flowers.
characters.voice: Young, soft and shy, gentle hesitant pace; female or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of a cauliflower with a dense white bumpy curd head wrapped in large green leaves
a close-up photo of knobbly cream-white cauliflower florets packed together like tiny trees
a photo of a winter vegetable cart stacked with white cauliflower heads surrounded by green leaves
a photo of a cauliflower cut in half showing thick white branching stalks under a grainy white top

lines.first_meet: [shyly] Phool gobi. Phool means flower, and I'm a tight bunch of baby flower buds. My leaves wrap me so I stay white.
lines.again: [blushing] Oh, you came back to see me? I'm still hiding in my leaves. But happy.
lines.goodbye: [softly] Bye. Go find a real flower in full bloom. It's braver than me.

characters.name: Band Gobi
characters.personality: A tight-lipped, mysterious type who shares exactly one layer at a time, and only with people who come back.
characters.voice: Adult, low and guarded, slow deliberate delivery; gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of a tight round cabbage head of overlapping smooth pale green leaves with visible veins
a photo of a cabbage cut in half showing tightly packed pale layered leaves around a white core
a photo of a vegetable cart piled with round smooth pale-green cabbages
a close-up photo of a cabbage's waxy smooth outer leaf curling over a firm round head

lines.first_meet: [mysteriously] Band gobi. Band means closed, and I am. Layer after layer, tight as a fist. Secrets inside, beta.
lines.again: [guarded] You again. All right. I'll share one more layer. Just one.
lines.goodbye: [closing up] Go open your eyes wide outside. Someone has to, since I won't.

characters.name: Gajar Lal
characters.personality: A cosy winter regular, crimson and proud, who believes every good grandmother's halwa owes him a thank-you.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, warm and homely, cosy and smiling; gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a photo of a winter cart piled with long tapering deep red-crimson carrots with feathery green tops
a close-up photo of thin dark crimson-red carrots with fine root hairs and faint ring lines
a photo of a red carrot cut across showing a crimson outside and a paler red core
a photo of a vendor's cart with a heap of red carrots beside a bucket of water

lines.first_meet: [warmly] Sindhi gajar! Deep red, only in winter. Every gajar ka halwa in Karachi starts with me and somebody's nani.
lines.again: [cosily] Back in winter again? I knew it. Halwa season brings everyone home.
lines.goodbye: [cheerfully] Go! Find the winter carts and look for my crimson heaps. Shawl recommended.

characters.name: Karela Kaka
characters.personality: A grumpy, bitter old soul with a secretly soft heart, who has made peace with the proverb written about him.
characters.voice: Older, grumbling and dry, reluctant warmth; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a close-up photo of a spindle-shaped dark green bitter gourd covered in warty ridges and bumps
a photo of a vegetable cart heap of knobbly green karela with pointed ends
a photo of a bitter gourd sliced into rings showing a white spongy centre and pale seeds
a photo of a climbing vine with deeply lobed leaves, small yellow flowers and hanging warty green gourds

lines.first_meet: [grumpy] Karela. Yes, bitter. There's even a saying: karela, and on top of that, it climbed a neem tree. Rude. Accurate.
lines.again: [grudgingly] You came back. To me. Willingly. Hm. That's... fine. Fine.
lines.goodbye: [grunts] Go away. Kindly. Go see a neem tree, then tell it I'm still more bitter.

characters.name: Lauki Ustad
characters.personality: A calm, musical soul whose dried relatives become sitars and water bottles; speaks gently and hums between sentences.
characters.voice: Mature, calm and mellow, soft humming pace; gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of long smooth pale-green bottle-shaped gourds with a narrow neck and a fat rounded bottom
a close-up photo of smooth matte pale-green lauki skin with fine soft fuzz and no warts or ridges
a photo of a vegetable cart stacked with long smooth club-shaped pale green gourds
a photo of a large gourd hanging from a vine on a rooftop trellis with broad velvety leaves and white flowers

lines.first_meet: [calmly] Lauki here. Dried, my family becomes water bottles and the round belly of a sitar. Not bad for a vegetable, na?
lines.again: [hums] Welcome back. Quiet, steady, still here. That's my whole style.
lines.goodbye: [softly hums] Go listen outside. Birds, wind, a rickshaw horn. Everything is a little music.

characters.name: Kaddu Khan
characters.personality: A jolly, round heavyweight who hears 'kaddu' as a compliment and spreads his vines like neighbourhood gossip.
characters.voice: Adult, jolly and round, rolling belly laugh; male or gender-neutral.
descriptions: a photo of a big round deeply ribbed orange pumpkin with a thick woody stem
a photo of green-mottled pumpkins and a cut wedge showing thick orange flesh on a vegetable cart
a close-up photo of hard deeply ribbed squash skin, green with orange patches
a photo of a pumpkin cut open showing dense bright orange flesh and a stringy centre of flat cream seeds

lines.first_meet: [jolly] Kaddu here! In Urdu, calling someone kaddu is an insult. I take it as praise: round, solid, dependable.
lines.again: [rolling laugh] Back again! You can't miss me. I'm the biggest thing on the cart.
lines.goodbye: [warmly] Go on, friend. Look for my wide vines sprawling over empty plots and walls. We spread out, like gossip.

characters.name: Bhutta Bhai
characters.personality: A smoky, crackling roadside showman who lives on the coal grill and smells the sea breeze before anyone else.
characters.voice: Young adult, warm and crackly, lively street-vendor energy; gender-neutral ok.
descriptions: a photo of corn cobs roasting over glowing coals on a street cart, kernels charred brown and yellow
a close-up photo of a cylindrical corn cob with neat straight rows of plump yellow kernels
a photo of whole corn cobs in green husks with brown silky tassels piled on a cart
a photo of a roasted corn cob rubbed with lemon and red chili masala, held by its husk

lines.first_meet: [sizzling] Bhutta here, fresh off the coals! Fun fact: every single kernel had its own silk thread. I'm hand-stitched.
lines.again: [crackles] You're back! Smell that smoke? That's me, waving.
lines.goodbye: [warmly] Go find the sea breeze, yaar. The best bhutta carts park wherever the wind is blowing.
